doc.title: Michael Max Fleming interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017

chapter: Mary Lou Williams and learning by ear
title: Why Ben Webster and Mary Lou Williams reacted as they did
summary: They discuss the lesson of the story, the unwritten rule of catching a tune by the second time around, and why Williams was embarrassed.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: It does. And it’s a perfect story because “Body and Soul” —
It is. And if you don’t know it, how do you know where that bridge is going to go, right?

Two years later I would have got to it. And with that whole thing it’s an unwritten rule that you know, if you hear something one time down you should be able to get enough of it and manage enough of it to be able to, second time around, do something with it.
I mean that’s with the people I know. I don’t know with somebody else. But I’m telling you that’s the level that I’ve operated at.
Okay. I think it’s really interesting that Mary Lou Williams said —
Oh see well don’t — see that’s why I started, I said don’t concentrate on that, that’s the story.
I know. But I like the way that she didn’t want to be, you embarrassed her.

Because what it is, see they go back, they go back to Kansas City. And so they had mutual respect. And so they’ve got a circle of, and I wasn’t in that circle, you know, but he’s coming to see her, I don’t know, maybe he flew in from Chicago or whatever. And you’ve got this little creep with you? The great Mary Lou and you can’t do better than this little greenhorn? It was like that.
